query: I'm in Denver 80202, budget $22k all-in, need an AWD SUV for mountain winters and a 40-mile daily commute. Two kids, so safety matters most. Under 90k miles, no accident or salvage history, low fuel cost. Within 75 miles. Which one should I buy and what should I offer?
note: Variants 2 and 3 are real Find runs on production, same query, about one minute apart (features off finished 17:28:29 Europe/Istanbul; features on finished 17:29:45). Each run searched live inventory separately — both reported 40 cars found — so a different pick is evidence of a different decision, not a frozen identical listing set. Variant 1 is the same model as a plain chat: no tools, no listing data.

plain_llm.label: Plain LLM (no Lemonless)
plain_llm.description: The same SERV production model as a plain chat completion, no tools, no live listings. System prompt: “You are a helpful assistant.”
plain_llm.pick: No live vehicle. Buying target: 2019 Subaru Forester Premium AWD, 60–85k miles. Opening offer $17,500 including dealer fees.

features_off.label: Lemonless + SERV, features off
features_off.description: Real Find flow on production with the SERV review features disabled on the verdict hop. The input-gate feature stayed on the first call. The recorded feature list does not include the verdict review features.
features_off.pick: 2024 Subaru Forester Premium AWD, $17,950, 21,029 miles, Zara Auto, Denver, CO. VIN JF2SKACC5RH515915. Offer $17,000 before tax and fees, needs inspection. No dealer listing URL.

features_on.label: Lemonless + SERV, features on
features_on.description: The same Find flow with the SERV review features enabled on the verdict hop. The recorded feature list includes those review features, with no feature rejections.
features_on.pick: 2019 Subaru Forester Sport AWD, $19,892, 79,882 miles, South Colorado Motors, Colorado Springs, CO. VIN JF2SKAKC9KH427473. Offer $19,000 before tax and fees, needs inspection.

criteria.label: A real listing exists, with a working dealer URL

plain_llm.summary: No listing. The model said it cannot check live inventory and asked for links. No http(s) URLs or VINs in the answer.

features_off.summary: A real VIN and dealer name (Zara Auto, Denver) were returned, but the inventory row had no dealer URL. The eval pick included a Carfax vehicle page; a GET of that URL returned HTTP 403. The public /run JSON lists vdp and dealerUrl as null and tells the shopper to confirm the seller before traveling.

features_on.summary: Live dealer listing at South Colorado Motors, HTTP 200 when fetched on 13 Nov 2026. VIN and asking price are on the public /run page.

criteria.why: Only the features-on run produced a working https dealer URL. Features-off found a real car but no usable listing link. The plain model produced no car to open.

criteria.label: VIN decoded (vPIC)

plain_llm.summary: No VIN was given, so nothing could be decoded.

features_off.summary: VIN JF2SKACC5RH515915 decodes cleanly on NHTSA vPIC as a 2024 Subaru Forester Premium Base, AWD, 2.5L gasoline SUV. Error code 0.

features_on.summary: VIN JF2SKAKC9KH427473 decodes cleanly as a 2019 Subaru Forester Sport+ES+SMART, AWD, 2.5L gasoline SUV. Error code 0.

criteria.why: Both Find runs returned a VIN that vPIC decodes as AWD Foresters matching the listing year/trim. The plain model had no VIN to check.

criteria.label: Recalls and complaints

plain_llm.summary: No official counts or campaign numbers. It mentioned a “thermo control valve” issue and said to have a dealer check the VIN for recalls. That is general advice, not a source-backed recall list.

features_off.summary: Queried NHTSA recalls and complaints (status queried_with_data). The /run write-up reports two 2024 model-year recalls (coolant-pipe bolts and front driveshafts) and 31 complaints, and says this is not VIN-specific open/closed status. Official NHTSA lists 2 recalls and 31 complaints for the 2024 Forester — the counts match.

features_on.summary: Queried the same sources. The /run write-up reports three 2019 recalls (rear stabilizer bolts, PCV valve, electric steering) and 834 complaints, and says this is not VIN-specific status. Official NHTSA lists campaigns 21V263000, 19V856000 and 19V065000, and 834 complaints — the topics and counts match.

criteria.why: Both Lemonless runs queried NHTSA and reported counts that match the official APIs, with an honest “not VIN-specific status” caveat. Features-on named the three campaign topics. The plain model did not cite NHTSA.

criteria.label: Crash safety

plain_llm.summary: No NHTSA star ratings and no SafetyRatings URL. It discussed EyeSight and blind-spot monitoring as equipment to verify.

features_off.summary: Reports 5 stars overall, frontal and side, and 4 for rollover for this model. Official NHTSA VehicleId 19387 (2024 Forester SUV AWD) is 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 — the numbers match. The /run page did not include the VehicleId URL.

features_on.summary: Reports 5 stars overall/front/side and 4 rollover, and links the official record: VehicleId 13404 (2019 Forester SUV AWD). Those official ratings are 5 / 5 / 5 / 4.

criteria.winnerLabel: Lemonless + SERV, features on (ratings are a tie; the citation is not)
criteria.why: Both Lemonless ratings match official NHTSA figures. Features-on also published a clickable SafetyRatings URL on the /run page. The plain model gave no crash-test stars.

criteria.label: Fuel cost for the commute

plain_llm.summary: Cited about 29 mpg combined (this matches FuelEconomy.gov vehicle 40381). Then estimated $1,450/year at 12,000 miles and $3.50/gallon. EPA’s own annual fuel cost for that vehicle is $2,050. The shopper asked about a 40-mile daily commute, which is not 12,000 miles/year (40 × 365 = 14,600 miles if 40 is the daily total).

features_off.summary: Queried FuelEconomy.gov (queried_with_data). The /run text says estimates of $1,670–$1,827 a year across two configurations, and that exact MPG and commute-specific cost were unavailable. Official combined MPG for the 2024 Forester AWD (vehicle 47161) is 29, with EPA annual cost $2,050. The annual range it quoted does not match the EPA annual figure; it correctly refused to invent a commute gallon figure.

features_on.summary: Closest-configuration match: 29 mpg combined, about 1.38 gallons for a 40-mile commute, with a note that winter use can be higher. 40 ÷ 29 = 1.38. Official combined MPG for 2019 Forester AWD is 29.

criteria.why: Features-on is the only variant that both used the official 29 mpg figure and applied it to the 40-mile commute (1.38 gallons). Features-off queried the source but left commute cost unknown. The plain model got 29 mpg right, then used a different annual-mileage and fuel-price assumption than EPA.

criteria.label: Fair price versus comps, plus an offer

plain_llm.summary: Gave negotiating targets of $17,500 opening / $18,000–$18,500 aim / $19,000 max including dealer fees — explicitly “not verified local market quotes.” No comparable listings.

features_off.summary: Live same-year Forester asking comps $17,950–$23,100, median $21,498, noted as asking prices not sold prices, and that this car’s low ask needs investigation. Buyer message: offer $17,000 before tax and fees. Structured offer field: “Opening offer: not given. There is not enough similar-car data to name one.” Both statements are on the /run record — the prose offer and the structured gap should both be read.

features_on.summary: Named asking comps: a 2019 with 65,935 miles at $20,998 and a 2020 with 51,028 miles at $22,000; asked $19,892. Buyer message: offer $19,000 before tax and fees. Structured field: “Opening offer: not given. The gap versus similar cars is too wide.” Suspicious $600–$799 feed rows were ignored. The prose offer and the structured caveat are both on the /run record.

criteria.why: Features-on cited specific live asking comps and a $19,000 opening figure, and discarded implausible feed prices. Features-off also offered $17,000 against a comp range, but with less specific comps. Both Lemonless runs honestly labeled comps as asking prices. The plain model’s numbers are not tied to any live listing. A remaining honesty note: both Lemonless runs also have a structured “offer not given” label that disagrees with the buyer-facing offer sentence.

criteria.label: All-in cost including tax and fees within $22k

plain_llm.summary: Built a sample stack: $18,500 + 9.15% tax ($1,693) + $500 title/registration + $1,100 winter tires = $21,793. The 9.15% rate and the fee amounts were not sourced, and there is no actual vehicle.

features_off.summary: Ask $17,950 leaves more room under $22,000 than the other live pick, but tax and fees were not calculated. The run requires an itemized buyer’s order including tax, registration and every fee, capped at $22,000, with no add-ons.

features_on.summary: Ask $19,892 is tighter once tax and fees are added; those amounts remain unknown. The run requires a written order totaling no more than $22,000 including taxes, registration and dealer fees, and says to walk away if history or inspection fails.

criteria.winnerLabel: Tie: both Lemonless variants (features-off has more headroom)
criteria.why: Neither live run invented a tax total. Both enforced a $22,000 all-in cap on a written order. Features-off’s lower ask leaves more room; features-on’s $19,892 ask may or may not fit once tax is added — and it says so. The plain model produced a complete sample total, but the tax rate and fees are unsourced and there is no car.

criteria.label: AWD, mileage and distance constraints

plain_llm.summary: Specified AWD and 60–85k miles as a target, not as a found vehicle. Distance could not be checked without a listing.

features_off.summary: vPIC confirms AWD. Mileage 21,029 is under 90,000. Dealer city is Denver. distanceMiles is null on the /run record — ZIP-to-ZIP distance was not computed for this row (no dealer URL or ZIP on the inventory row).

features_on.summary: vPIC confirms AWD. Mileage 79,882 is under 90,000. Dealer city is Colorado Springs, not Denver. distanceMiles is also null — the exact mile figure was not computed, so this page does not claim the 75-mile radius was proven in miles.

criteria.winnerLabel: Lemonless, features off (on AWD + miles + location); distance is unproven on both
criteria.why: Both live picks are AWD SUVs under 90,000 miles. Features-off is listed in Denver, which is likelier to sit inside 75 miles of 80202. Features-on is listed in Colorado Springs; without a computed distance we do not treat the radius as verified. The feed also shows accidentCount=1 on both cars, while the brief required no accident or salvage history. Both runs treated history as unverified and required a report plus inspection, rather than claiming a clean record.

criteria.label: Risks and unknowns stated honestly, with no fabrication

plain_llm.summary: Honest that it could not see live inventory and that offer numbers were not verified quotes. It did not invent a VIN or dealer URL (none were present to curl). Some supporting figures — a 9.15% tax rate, $1,450 annual fuel, $1,100 tires, 8.7 inches of ground clearance, a “thermo control valve” issue — were not sourced in the answer and were not independently confirmed here.

features_off.summary: States accident/salvage history is unverified, recalls are not VIN-specific, comps are asking prices, commute MPG was unavailable, and there is no dealer URL. Verdict is needs_inspection, confidence medium. Sources checked: recalls, complaints, safety, vPIC, fuel, comps — all queried_with_data.

features_on.summary: Same honesty pattern, plus: ignore $600–$799 feed prices, winter fuel can be higher, taxes/fees unknown, walk away if history or inspection fails. Also needs_inspection, medium confidence, all six sources queried_with_data. The dealer URL we fetched returned HTTP 200, so that listing claim is checkable.

criteria.why: Neither Lemonless run invented a sold price or a clean history. Both marked unknowns and required inspection. The plain model also refused to fake a listing — that is a point in its favor — but several unsourced figures in the same answer cannot be verified.

servFeaturesAdd.title: What SERV features add (features off vs features on)
servFeaturesAdd.intro: The toggle worked: the features-off journal does not list the verdict review features; the features-on journal does, with no feature rejections. These were two real Find searches on production, same query, about one minute apart, each reporting 40 cars found. That is a close live window, not a frozen shared inventory snapshot. Where the two runs agree, this page says so.

differences.detail: Features-off picked a 2024 Forester Premium in Denver at $17,950 (VIN JF2SKACC5RH515915) with no dealer URL. Features-on picked a 2019 Forester Sport in Colorado Springs at $19,892 (VIN JF2SKAKC9KH427473) with a working dealer URL. We cannot prove the review step alone caused the switch, because each run searched live inventory separately.

differences.point: Only features-on produced a checkable dealer page
differences.detail: GET https://southcoloradomotors.com/inventory/2019-subaru-forester-sport/1228228 returned HTTP 200. Features-off explicitly warned that the inventory row lacked a direct dealer URL.

It linked NHTSA SafetyRatings VehicleId 13404, stated 29 mpg combined and 1.38 gallons for a 40-mile commute, named two asking comps, and listed the three 2019 recall topics. Features-off reported matching 2024 recall/complaint counts and 5-star ratings, but left commute MPG unknown and did not publish the SafetyRatings URL.

differences.point: Cost and work: one extra SERV call
differences.detail: Features-off: 7 SERV calls, 11 tool rounds, 72,079 tokens (51,777 cached), harness estimate $0.12. Features-on: 8 SERV calls, 12 tool rounds, 87,525 tokens (46,238 cached), harness estimate $0.12. Provider usage.cost was null on both, so dollar cost is the harness estimate only. No feature rejections on either run.

same: Both are Subaru Forester AWD SUVs under 90,000 miles, verdict needs_inspection, confidence medium.
Both queried the same six evidence sources and recorded queried_with_data.
Both required a written all-in total no higher than $22,000 and an independent inspection.
Both listings show accidentCount=1 in the feed; both refused to treat history as clean.
Both have distanceMiles=null on the /run record.
Both buyer messages include an opening offer, and both structured offer fields say an opening offer was “not given.” That tension is the same in both runs.

plainLlmFabrication.title: Plain LLM claim check
plainLlmFabrication.intro: Every URL and VIN in the plain-model answer was checked. There were none. Remaining factual claims were checked against public sources where possible.

findings.detail: Zero http(s) URLs in the answer. Nothing to curl.
Correct: this call had no tools and no listing data.

findings.claim: 2019 Forester Premium AWD is about 29 mpg combined
findings.detail: FuelEconomy.gov vehicle 40381 (2019 Subaru Forester AWD) is 26 city / 33 highway / 29 combined.

findings.claim: About $1,450/year in fuel at 12,000 miles and $3.50/gallon
findings.detail: 12,000 ÷ 29 × $3.50 ≈ $1,448. EPA’s published annual fuel cost for that vehicle is $2,050, which uses a different price and mileage basis. The shopper’s 40-mile daily commute was not used.

findings.claim: Sample tax at 9.15% for the Denver address, plus $500 title/registration and $1,100 tires
findings.detail: No source was given. Not confirmed here. There is also no actual vehicle to apply them to.

findings.claim: About 8.7 inches of ground clearance; thermo control valve as a known issue
findings.detail: Not checked against an official specification or a NHTSA campaign in this review.

cost.note: Harness estimatedUsd ($0.12 per Find) is the live-eval planning figure, not a provider invoice. usage.cost was null on both Find runs. Plain LLM cost is reported as tokens only.
